title: Word Detail — root nzl across 2:23 and 17:106
_script: [0:00–0:05]  RootPage. Narration: 'The Quranic root nūn-zay-lām means to descend, to send down from above.'
[0:05–0:11]  VerseFlow 2:23. Narration: 'In Sūrah al-Baqarah, verse 23, this root takes its intensive form: nazzalnā — We have sent down.'
[0:11–0:18]  WordToWord 2:23. Narration: 'The verse is the famous challenge: if you doubt what We sent, produce a sūrah like it.'
[0:18–0:26]  VerseFlow 17:106. Narration: 'And in chapter 17, the same root makes the descent explicit — sent down piece by piece, over time.'

slides.meaning: To descend, to send down from above

slides.arabicText: وَإِن كُنتُمْ فِى رَيْبٍ مِّمَّا نَزَّلْنَا عَلَىٰ عَبْدِنَا فَأْتُوا۟ بِسُورَةٍ مِّن مِّثْلِهِۦ وَٱدْعُوا۟ شُهَدَآءَكُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ إِن كُنتُمْ صَٰدِقِينَ
slides.translation: And if you are in doubt about what We have sent down upon Our servant, then bring a sūrah from the like of it.
If you doubt what We sent down upon Our servant, bring a sūrah like it.

slides.arabicText: وَقُرْءَانًا فَرَقْنَـٰهُ لِتَقْرَأَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلنَّاسِ عَلَىٰ مُكْثٍ وَنَزَّلْنَـٰهُ تَنزِيلًا
slides.translation: A Qurʾān We have set out in stages, to be read to people gradually — sent down piece by piece.

slides.tagline: A Root Based Translation of the Quran
